For a while now, my team and I have been playing this game from computers at a gaming lounge. This means none of us can or would ever cheat—first, because we completely disagree with these methods, and second, because the lounge is strictly regulated by rules and terms where cheating results in heavy financial penalties and other serious consequences. Despite all of this, the game banned us under the accusation of cheating, even though we are completely incapable of it and have never cheated. We play inside a controlled environment that follows strict regulations. The most frustrating part is that actual cheaters are still playing normally, while innocent players who never cheat get banned. I honestly don't understand how paying customers who play fairly are treated this way. Because of this, we have decided to stop playing this game entirely. Thank you very much

I personally believe that players have continued to play the game solely on the strength of the anime IP Edgerunners. Frankly, however, if Cyberpunk 2077 were a film rather than a game, its captivating narrative would be thoroughly immersive: the side quests endow characters—from the lower to the upper strata of Night City, from V’s friends to V’s enemies—with flesh and blood, making players feel as though they are living alongside genuinely existing individuals in such a bizarre and dazzling city; the main storyline, for its part, firmly captures V’s real predicament, prompting players to actively advance the plot and even to imagine themselves living in Night City, this futuristic metropolis.
